=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:6523-7757 | severity=high | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna]
  PROBLEM: The advisory recorder can return success when building or persisting waiver rows fails, and the caller does not check for failure before marking an advisory-only audit result passed.
  WHY: The failed write leaves no waiver or follow-up record while the audited head may be marked passed; reviewers disagree whether a subsequent same-head poll skips the audit or reruns it.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:6523 | severity=low | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro]
  PROBLEM: `--argjson defer "${defer}"` is passed to `jq`, but the expression no longer references `$defer`.
  WHY: `jq` silently ignores the unused variable, so this is dead-code cleanup only and does not fail at runtime.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:7291 | severity=high | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [qwen_qwen3_7-plus]
  PROBLEM: `security_pass_exhaustion_judge` reads `${advisory_count:-0}` even though `advisory_count` is local to its caller and is not passed to the function.
  WHY: Bash does not expose a caller's local variable to a called function, so the exhaustion-judge path reports `advisory=0` regardless of the actual advisory count, contrary to the documentation at agents.md:1588.

=== FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:6523 | severity=NIT | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The `--argjson defer "${defer}"` parameter is passed to `jq` but the expression no longer references `$defer` after the last autofix removed the conditional `+ (if $defer then ... else {} end)` block. The shell variable `defer` remains in use (line 6552), but the jq variable is dead.
  WHY: It does not — `jq` ignores unused top-level variables silently. This is a dead-code cosmetic issue only.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:7731 (call) → 6543 (return from security_pass_record_waivers failure) | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: `security_pass_record_line_ownership_advisories` calls `security_pass_record_waivers` and, on failure, emits a warning and returns 0. The caller at line 7731 does not inspect the return value. If `security_pass_record_waivers` fails, the waiver rows are not persisted in state, but the findings file has already been stripped of advisory entries (the `mv "${findings_file}.blocking" "${findings_file}"` at line 7730 succeeded). The subsequent state write at line 7751 sees `finding_count == 0` and records `security_pass_status: "passed"` plus `security_pass_head_sha` without the waiver data.
  WHY: The advisory findings are in neither `security_pass_waived_findings` nor `security_pass_reported_findings`. On the next poll tick the pass sees the same head marked passed and skips without re-auditing. The waiver-suppression dedupe cannot fire because nothing was recorded. The only recovery is a later head advance that triggers a delta audit, which re-reports the findings (they are not suppressed without waiver rows) and the split/record is retried. The function is documented as fail-open by design, and the comment block at lines 6505-6507 describes this behaviour. Recovery is eventual rather than immediate, but it does exist.
=== END FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===

=== FINDINGS FROM google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite ===
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:6523-6526 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The function security_pass_record_line_ownership_advisories returns 0 (success) even when recording waiver rows to the state fails.
  WHY: The caller run_security_pass_inline proceeds as if the advisories were successfully recorded. If recording fails, the system might erroneously record the head as passed without ensuring the follow-up state is persisted, leading to potential inconsistency where advisories are not properly tracked for future audits.
=== END FINDINGS FROM google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite ===

=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh: security_pass_record_line_ownership_advisories() function (original PR diff lines 6489-6579), specifically the failure paths at the jq-build warning (around the "Could not build line-ownership advisory rows" echo) and the security_pass_record_waivers warning (around the "Could not record line-ownership advisories" echo); called from run_security_pass_inline() in the advisory split block (original PR diff around lines 7711-7735) | severity=MAJOR | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The helper returns 0 (success) on both the jq-build failure path and the security_pass_record_waivers failure path after only emitting a ::warning::. The caller in run_security_pass_inline does not check the helper's exit code, so it proceeds as if recording succeeded. In the advisory-only case the poller then records the audited head as passed without storing the waiver rows in security_pass_waived_findings, without filing any deferred follow-up issues, and without posting the "🔐 Security-pass advisory findings (pre-existing code)" tracking comment. Operators lose visibility into which pre-existing-code findings were suppressed for that audit cycle.
  WHY: The deferred filer (security_pass_file_deferred_advisory_followups, called at the final merge) relies on followup_pending waiver rows to retry unfiled follow-ups; if security_pass_record_waivers itself failed, no such row exists, so no retry happens. The next poll cycle still re-runs the audit (the cross-pollination summary's "skips the audit" claim is wrong -- audits run every cycle in this path), and re-reports and re-records the same advisories, but the operator visibility for THIS audit cycle is lost. A persistent state-write failure across multiple cycles would mask the advisory set indefinitely until the underlying write issue is fixed, and the tracking comment for the previous cycle was never posted so operators have no record of what was suppressed. The LAST RUN DIFF removed the secondary jq write that previously set followup_pending in a second state pass, which is the right simplification, but it did not address this deeper failure path.
=== END FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===

=== FINDINGS FROM openai_gpt-6-luna ===
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:6543-6545, 7731, 7755-7757, 7387-7388 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: Failure to persist line-ownership advisory rows is ignored, and the audited head is still recorded as passed when no blocking findings remain.
  WHY: If security_pass_record_waivers fails, security_pass_record_line_ownership_advisories warns and returns success. The caller does not check persistence and continues to mark an advisory-only result passed at the current head. On the next poll, security_pass_current_head_is_valid accepts that head and skips the audit. With no waiver or pending follow-up row in state, the advisory is neither filed nor retried.
=== END FINDINGS FROM openai_gpt-6-luna ===

=== FINDINGS FROM qwen_qwen3_7-plus ===
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:7291 (in security_pass_exhaustion_judge), called from 7809 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The exhaustion judge function uses `${advisory_count:-0}` at line 7291, but `advisory_count` is a local variable in the calling function `run_security_pass_inline` (declared at line 7356) and is not passed as a parameter to `security_pass_exhaustion_judge`. The function signature at lines 6959-6971 shows only 7 parameters, none of which is `advisory_count`.
  WHY: In bash, local variables in a calling function are not accessible in called functions. The `${advisory_count:-0}` expression will always evaluate to `0` in the exhaustion judge path, regardless of the actual advisory count. The documentation at agents.md:1588 states that `SECURITY_PASS_CLEAN` gains `advisory=<n>` on both main and exhaustion-judge paths, but the exhaustion judge will always report `advisory=0`.
=== END FINDINGS FROM qwen_qwen3_7-plus ===
